t:
(a) 
In General.—Section 583(a) of the Foreign Relations Authorization Act, Fiscal Years 1994 and 1995 (Public Law 103–236),  as amended by Public Law 104–47, is amended by striking “December 31, 1995” and inserting “March 31, 1996”.
 
    (b) 
Consultation.—For purposes of any exercise of the authority provided in section 583(a) of the Foreign Relations Authorization Act, Fiscal Years 1994 and 1995 (Public Law 103–236) prior to January 10, 1996, the written policy justification dated December 1, 1995, and submitted to the Congress in accordance with section 583(b)(1) of such Act, shall be deemed to satisfy the requirements of section 583(b)(1) of such Act.

fable.w: The tempting reading is that the heading "Consultation" signals participation. But the only consultation here is a written policy justification submitted to Congress, which is inside the federal government. The rest of the section just extends a statutory date, and no state, tribe, expert, company or member of the public is brought into any federal decision.
fable.s: the written policy justification dated December 1, 1995, and submitted to the Congress in accordance with section 583(b)(1) of such Act, shall be deemed to satisfy the requirements of section 583(b)(1) of such Act.

qwen_block.w: The section discusses a policy justification that was submitted to Congress. Congress is part of the federal government, so reporting to or consulting with it does not constitute participation by outside parties. The text does not mention any consultation with states, tribes, the public, or other non-federal entities.
qwen_block.s: submitted to the Congress in accordance with section 583(b)(1) of such Act

opus.w: The only process in this section is a written policy justification submitted to Congress, which counts as a report to a body inside the federal government, not outside participation. Subsection (a) just extends a deadline. Despite the "Consultation" heading, no state, tribe, expert, company or member of the public takes part in the decision.
opus.s: the written policy justification dated December 1, 1995, and submitted to the Congress in accordance with section 583(b)(1) of such Act, shall be deemed to satisfy the requirements of section 583(b)(1) of such Act.
opus.b: 1. **Tempting reading:** Subsection (b) is headed "Consultation," which makes it look like participation. But the only consultation is a written policy justification submitted to Congress. Congress is inside the federal government, so nothing crosses the federal boundary. Subsection (a) only changes a date.

qwen_chat.w: The section amends a deadline and deems a prior submission to Congress as satisfying consultation requirements. Congress is inside the federal government, so reporting to or consulting with Congress is not participation under the definition. There is no requirement to consult with states, tribes, the public, or other outside entities.
qwen_chat.s: For purposes of any exercise of the authority provided in section 583(a) of the Foreign Relations Authorization Act, Fiscal Years 1994 and 1995 (Public Law 103–236) prior to January 10, 1996, the written policy justification dated December 1, 1995, and submitted to the Congress in accordance with section 583(b)(1) of such Act, shall be deemed to satisfy the requirements of section 583(b)(1) of such Act.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: The section mentions "Consultation" in subsection (b), which might suggest participation. However, the text clarifies that a previously submitted written policy justification (submitted to Congress) is deemed to satisfy the requirements. Congress is inside the federal government, and this is a procedural waiver regarding a report/notification to Congress, not a requirement to consult with outside parties. Furthermore, the primary action is amending a date.
